447: Built around Huron Blackheart, Abaddon, Chosen, Defilers, and waves of Cultist Mob bodies screened by Masters of the Maelstrom, this is a mass-horde siege army running Fellhammer Siege-Host in the majority of lists, which subtracts 1 from wound rolls whenever an attacker's Strength exceeds the target's Toughness — making the whole force stubbornly durable against high-Strength shooting. The plan is to flood the board with cheap bodies holding objectives while Chosen and Defilers grind forward under that wound-roll protection, using Dark Pacts through the Cabal of Chaos secondary detachment to punch up on key targets in both the shooting and fight phases. It punishes gunline armies that rely on volume high-Strength fire to clear infantry efficiently, since the Fellhammer modifier bleeds damage off almost every common anti-horde weapon profile. Where it cracks is precise, low-Strength high-volume shooting or mortal wound generation that bypasses wound rolls entirely, stripping Cultists faster than Huron's horde can re-establish board presence.
448: Built around Cultist Mobs, Defilers, Venomcrawlers, Forgefiends, Vashtorr the Arkifane, and Warpsmiths, this list runs the Cabal of Chaos detachment with Soulforged Warpack as a secondary, flooding the board with Heretic Astartes Daemon Vehicles executing Dark Pacts to gain +1 to Wound on ranged attacks and a surge of extra melee Attacks. The win condition is overwhelming anti-armour pressure — Dark Pact-fuelled Defilers and Forgefiends crack hard targets at range while Venomcrawlers threaten mid-table brawls, with Vashtorr and Warpsmiths keeping the engines operational and feeding the Pact economy. It punishes mechanised lists and heavy armour concentrations brutally, stacking mobile anti-armour output that most vehicle-heavy armies cannot trade into efficiently. It cracks against elite infantry and screen-heavy builds that absorb the Daemon Engines in melee while denying clean Pact targets, exposing how thin the scoring footprint becomes when Cultist Mobs get removed early.
450: Built around Lady Malys, Drazhar, Lelith Hesperax, Wyches, and Incubi packed into Raiders and Venoms, this is a transport-heavy Wych Cult swarm running Exhibition Of Slaughter and Skysplinter Assault together. The engine is a coordinated disembark alpha: units pile out of skimmers to hit with Lance melee and Ignores Cover shooting, while Exhibition Of Slaughter grants Lethal Hits on all Wych Cult melee attacks against non-Monster, non-Vehicle targets, turning even chaff Wyches into blenders on the charge. It punishes infantry-dense lists brutally — the sheer volume of Lethal Hits attacks across four average Wych squads plus Incubi and named characters overwhelms saves and forces catastrophic morale math. Armies that can strip transports at range before the disembark trigger, particularly anti-skimmer lists with high flat-damage shooting, crack this open by denying the Lance and Ignores Cover payoff entirely.
466:
Built around Flawless Blades, Infractors, Lords Exultant, Tormentors, Defilers, Winged Daemon Princes, and Fulgrim, this is a transport-heavy mid-table brawler running Coterie of the Conceited — a detachment that rewards you for accurately predicting how many enemy units you'll kill each round, converting successful pledges into Pact points.

The engine is momentum-based kill efficiency: surge forward in Rhinos, crash into multiple combats simultaneously, and make conservative-but-meaningful pledges to steadily bank Pact points while contesting midfield objectives with durable, mobile infantry.

It punishes slower gunlines and anything that surrenders multiple small units per turn, since each kill feeds the pledge mechanic while the sheer volume of threats — ground walkers, flying Princes, elite melee infantry — creates severe target-priority stress.

Aggressive alpha-strike armies that can dismantle the transport layer and reduce your kill volume below your pledge threshold crack it open, as a failed pledge nets nothing, stalling the Pact engine at the worst possible moment.
473: Built around Paladin Squads, Brotherhood Terminator Squads, Grand Master Voldus, a Brotherhood Chaplain, and Strike Squads delivered by a Land Raider Redeemer, this is a mobile melee-toolbox army running Argent Assault. The core engine is Paladin Squads crashing into high-Toughness targets and gaining +1 to wound when their Strength would otherwise fall short, letting them punch through armor that should bounce them, while Brotherhood Terminators and Interceptors flex across the board to contest objectives and pick secondary fights. It punishes static, elite armies that cluster valuable units together, because the combination of Paladins overcoming Toughness thresholds and Chaplain support creates compounding melee pressure that those lists cannot trade efficiently against. It cracks when faced with extreme volume fire or fast armies that strip screens before the Redeemer delivers its payload, leaving the Paladins isolated and unable to leverage their wound-roll advantage.
481: Built around the Knight Castellan, this list is a Dominus Foebreakers build that exploits the detachment's +1 to hit rolls against units in terrain, turning the Castellan's massed firepower into a punishment engine for any opponent who hides in cover. The win condition is simple: saturate terrain-hugging targets with accurate, high-volume heavy shooting while the Gate Warden Lance's defensive line locks down two objectives, forcing the opponent to come to you and walk into the Castellan's sights. It punishes armour-heavy lists and elite infantry sheltering in ruins, where the hit bonus stacks onto already-punishing weapons to create anti-tank overload that few durable targets can absorb. It cracks open against highly mobile, low-footprint armies that contest in the open and deny terrain play, or fast melee threats that can close and lock the Castellan in combat before it unloads.
480: Built around Armiger Warglaives, Armiger Helverins, and a Knight Castellan, this list fields a swarm of fast medium Knights backed by a single apocalyptic centerpiece, with Spearhead-at-Arms allowing Bondsman abilities to buff up to three Armigers simultaneously and turning the entire pack into a synchronized strike package. The win condition is layered anti-armour pressure — Helverins pepper targets at range while Warglaives close and threaten multiple flanks, forcing opponents to split resources across too many high-wound threats to reliably neutralize. It punishes armour-heavy lists brutally, as the sheer volume of high-strength, multi-damage shooting and melee from the Armiger swarm overloads anti-tank resources and creates no safe target priority. However, elite infantry screens and dense terrain deny the mobility-dependent Armigers clean engagement angles, and without durable objective holders, it struggles to convert kill efficiency into consistent scoring against disciplined screen-and-deny armies.
430: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Hekaton Land Fortress, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and a deep supporting cast of Kâhl, Hernkyn Pioneers, Kapricus Carriers, and Hearthkyn Warriors, this list runs the Hearthguard Covenant detachment to squeeze re-rolls of wound rolls of 1 on ranged attacks within 9" out of its elite core. The plan is to close the mid-board fast, stack bodies on objectives, and grind enemies off points through sheer attrition — Hernkyn Yaegirs and Pioneers screen and harass while the Hearthguard and Thunderkyn deliver massed short-range firepower. It punishes slower, less durable armies that can't match its combined arms volume, especially lists that fold under layered anti-infantry and anti-tank pressure from multiple angles simultaneously. Aggressive alpha-strike armies that can strip the forward screen and isolate Hearthguard before they close to 9" range break the wound re-roll engine before it ever fires.
482: Built around Armiger Warglaives, the Knight Castellan, Knight Crusader, Cerastus Knight Lancer, and Armiger Helverins, this is a full-blooded Knights army running Freeblade Company for its passive wound regeneration and army-wide Feel No Pain 6+, making every model on the table meaningfully harder to grind down. The plan is to layer heavy anti-armour firepower from the Castellan and Crusader into high-value targets while the Lancers and Warglaives apply mobile pressure across the board, accumulating attrition advantages that translate into objective control as the enemy's heavy hitters evaporate. It punishes lists that rely on focused damage to remove individual threats, since the wound-regain engine means a Knight that survives a shooting phase comes back slightly healthier each Command phase, extending its effective lifespan well beyond what opponents plan for. Its weakness is volume of high-AP, high-damage output — armies that can simultaneously threaten multiple Knights force difficult choices, and without significant screening infantry, a coordinated alpha strike can cripple the army before regeneration ever matters.
456: Built around Canoptek Wraiths, Ophydian Destroyers, Technomancers, Skorpekh Lords, and C'tan Shards of the Void Dragon and the Nightbringer — all running Awakened Dynasty, where every CHARACTER-led unit gains +1 to Hit — this list floods the board with fast, durable melee threats backed by Illuminor Szeras and Canoptek Reanimators keeping key units cycling back into play. The win condition is relentless multi-angle pressure: Ophydian Destroyers and Wraiths collapse opponent screens while C'tan Shards crash into hard targets, scoring through board control and attrition rather than any single kill chain. It punishes slower, lower-volume armies that can't handle simultaneous threats across multiple vectors, as spreading damage thin against regenerating models bleeds opponents dry. It cracks against heavy-shooting lists that can isolate and delete individual threats before the reanimation engine catches up, since losing key buffers like the Reanimator early collapses the whole recovery loop.
486: Built around near-maximum Boyz squads, Painboys, Warbosses, Bigbosses, Ghazghkull Thraka, and Wazdakka Gutsmek under the Green Tide detachment, this is an oppressive mass-horde army that floods the board with bodies backed by character stacking. The win condition is drowning the midfield in Boyz blobs of 10+ models — triggering the 5+ invulnerable save — while Painboys keep those blobs alive long enough for Ghazghkull and Warboss/Bigboss combos to deliver crushing melee output turn after turn. It punishes low-model-count elite armies mercilessly, trading cheap wounds efficiently while characters amplify damage to levels elite units cannot absorb. Anything with high-volume mortal wounds, blast weapons, or strong overwatch dismantles the horde math before it reaches combat.
487: Built around Mozrog Skragbad, Beastbosses on Squigosaurs, Squighog Boyz, Beast Snagga Boyz, Kill Rigs, and Gretchin screens, this is a Da Big Hunt list that designates a high-value enemy unit as Prey each Command phase and chains Beast Snagga charge re-rolls into a relentless mid-table brawl. The win condition is simple brutality: lock the Prey unit in combat using re-rolling charges across multiple Beast Snagga units simultaneously, grinding the opponent's key pieces off the board while Kill Rigs and Squighogs apply mobile anti-armour pressure and Gretchin hold backfield objectives. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that lack the board presence to screen against multiple fast, re-rolling charges landing from different angles on a single target. Armies with deep-strike denial tools, strong shooting at range, or durable screens that can absorb the charge phase without crumbling will buy enough time to blunt the assault before the Orks can cycle into a second wave.
468: Built around Vulkan He'stan, multiple Infernus Squads, Librarians, Land Raider Redeemers, Bladeguard Veterans, Adrax Agatone, Scout Squads, and Sternguard Veterans, this Forgefather's Seekers list is a transport-delivered close-range fire platform that turns every Astartes ranged weapon into an Assault weapon and pumps Strength by 1 within 12". The win condition is rolling Redeemers into midboard, dumping Infernus and Sternguard at point-blank range, and burning through both infantry and armour with He'stan's Seeker's Companions unlocking Infernus Squad objective play while Librarians cycle Psychic Disciplines — Divination for reliability, Pyromancy for raw heat — to amplify each combat phase. It absolutely punishes medium-toughness infantry hordes and lightly armoured vehicle spam that cannot survive massed short-range S5+ fire before it can establish scoring positions. Armies that can alpha-strike the Redeemers before they deliver their cargo, or screen with cheap bodies to deny the 12" engagement range, expose how dependent this list is on surviving the approach.
488: Built around multiple Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Lootas, Flash Gitz, Tankbustas, and Big Mek Dakkarigs hauled forward in Trukks, all operating under the Dread Mob detachment's randomised-or-chosen weapon ability dice engine alongside More Dakka!'s Assault and Waaagh!-fuelled Sustained Hits 1 on infantry. The plan is to flood mid-board with Gretchin screens while Trukks deliver Tankbustas and Flash Gitz into threat range, letting the Shokk Attack Guns and Lootas saturate the backfield with concentrated fire that spikes hard during an active Waaagh!. It punishes static gunlines and lightly screened armour by combining anti-tank overload from Tankbustas with the sheer volume of Dread Mob-buffed shots, making efficient target prioritisation nearly impossible for the opponent. Elite low-model-count lists that can alpha strike through the Gretchin chaff and surgically eliminate the Trukk payloads before Waaagh! activates crack it open fastest.
467: Built around Marneus Calgar in the Armour of Antilochus, Victrix Honour Guard, Ballistus Dreadnoughts, and Repulsor Executioners, this Blade of Ultramar list plays a disciplined gunline backed by a resilient melee anchor. Calgar's ability to recycle Combat Doctrines keeps the army's buffs cycling throughout the game, while Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreads pour sustained heavy fire into priority targets as Scouts and Intercessors lock down objectives. The list punishes slow, durable armies that rely on holding ground — the combination of heavy vehicle firepower and mobile Jump Pack Intercessors creates anti-armour overload that static defensive lists cannot answer from multiple angles simultaneously. It cracks under pressure from aggressive alpha-strike armies that can isolate and kill Calgar early, collapsing the doctrine engine and leaving the gunline without its key force-multiplier.
478: Built around Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Logan Grimnar, Arjac Rockfist, Wolf Guard Terminators, Thunderwolf Cavalry, Wulfen with storm shields, Intercessors, and Gladiator Lancers, this is a mid-table brawler running either Saga of the Great Wolf or Saga of the Beastslayer depending on matchup. The plan is to crash Thunderwolves and Terminators led by Grimnar and Arjac into the midboard while Bjorn and Lancers provide fire support, using transport-loaded Intercessors to hold secondary objectives and funnel scoring through sustained combat presence. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't absorb repeated charges from multiple durable melee threats hitting simultaneously across several turns. However, the lack of a single dominant detachment ability and the moderate anti-armour output leave it exposed against heavily mechanised gunlines that can strip the cavalry screen before the brawl ever develops.
428: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinder Teams, Riptides, Broadsides, Ghostkeels, Piranhas, and the Twin Lance, this is a mobile gunline that weaponizes the Mont'ka detachment's [ASSAULT] and [LETHAL HITS] rules across the first three battle rounds to shoot after advancing and convert hits into wounds with lethal efficiency while Pathfinders enable Guided units to stack that lethality on priority targets. The plan is to advance aggressively into scoring positions turn one, maintain Guidance chains, and delete armoured threats through sheer anti-tank volume before the enemy stabilises. It punishes vehicle-heavy and monster-heavy lists badly — Broadsides and Riptides pumping Lethal Hits into heavy targets is a genuine kill chain that overwraps traditional T-tough defences. Where it struggles is against armies that can deny or disrupt the Guidance network early, collapsing the Lethal Hits payoff and leaving the shooting merely adequate rather than devastating.
483: Built around Biovores, Neurolictors, a Neurotyrant, Broodlord, Genestealers, Hyperadapted Raveners, Deathleaper, Zoanthropes, Lictors, and Von Ryan's Leapers, this is a swarming infiltration army that floods every corner of the board with independently threatening units before the game even begins. The win condition is simultaneous pressure: Neurolictors and Lictors deny safe deployment and peel screens, creating corridors for Genestealers and Hyperadapted Raveners to crack open mid-table and score Primary through sheer board saturation while Biovores chip backfield units off objectives. It punishes static, low-model-count armies that lack redundant screens, because the sheer volume of infiltrating threats forces impossible prioritisation decisions turn one. Armies with reliable board-wide blast damage or strong pre-game screening — anything that can clog the infiltration lanes or wipe genestealer packs before they make contact — expose how fragile the individual pieces are once the initial momentum stalls.
490: Built around Sekhetar Robots, Defilers, Forgefiends, Tzaangor Shamans, and Exalted Sorcerers on Discs, this is a psyker-buffed heavy gunline that leans hard into robot-and-vehicle synergy — Shamans and Sorcerers orbit the Robots to grant +1 WS on melee attacks while making every attack Psychic, and Warpforged Cabal lets adjacent psykers unlock full re-roll packages on Vehicle shooting. The plan is to establish board dominance through layered anti-armour firepower, using Forgefiends and Defilers supported by psyker auras to grind down opposing vehicles and elite infantry while Sekhetar Robots threaten both at range and in melee. It punishes mechanised lists brutally — the combination of mobile anti-armour output and Psychic-tagged attacks with enhanced WS means armoured or high-toughness targets rarely survive sustained engagement. Screens, elite melee counter-charges, and armies that can push psykers off the Robots early disrupt the buff engine and collapse the damage chain.
489: Built around Sekhetar Robots (nearly three squads deep), Scarab Occult Terminators, Tzaangor Enlightened with fatecaster greatbows, Rubric Marines, Tzaangors, and a Daemon Prince with wings, this Hexwarp Thrallband list floods the board with bodies and layers psychic-buffed firepower across multiple threat vectors. The engine is Flow of Magic control: by contesting No Man's Land objectives early, the list unlocks mid-board phase buffs, then uses Sekhetar Cohort's Infusion aura through Psyker characters to pump Robot melee WS, turning objective fights into a grind the opponent simply can't win on attrition. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that can't clear the sheer volume of wounds efficiently, while Enlightened skimmer fire picks apart light screens at range. Armies with high-volume mortal wound output or powerful alpha-strike deepstrike threats can crack the flow of Magic tempo before it establishes, unraveling the buff chain before it pays off.
427: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinder Teams, Ghostkeels, and a deep roster of Crisis variants — Starscythes, Fireknives, Sunforges — alongside Riptides, Coldstar Commanders, Commander Farsight, and The Twin Lance, this list operates from the Advanced Acquisition Cadre detachment, where Pathfinders and Stealth Battlesuits remain hidden even after shooting. The engine is persistent board presence: hidden units bait opponents into suboptimal trades while the Crisis swarm and Riptides close range to trigger Retaliation Cadre's Strength and AP buffs inside 12" and 8". It punishes armour-heavy lists mercilessly — nine-plus mobile anti-armour platforms stacking close-range AP improvements systematically overload elite vehicles and monsters. Armies that can strip hidden status early or flood the midboard with cheap bodies to contest Crisis positioning before those range bands close will crack the scoring engine apart.
484: Built around Norn Assimilators, Norn Emissaries, Pyrovores, Psychophages, Ripper Swarms, and Biovores, this list runs the Assimilation Swarm detachment and leans hard into HARVESTER-fueled regeneration — returning slain Infantry models and healing wounded Monstrous Creatures every Command phase to grind opponents into attrition loops. The win condition is sustained mid-board pressure: park regenerating blobs and monsters on objectives, deny removal through constant body recycling, and let Biovores punish backfield screens while Norn engines flex across the table with Protean Purpose adaptability. It punishes armies that rely on incremental chip damage and low-volume elite shooting, since regeneration neutralises that kill-before-scoring plan entirely. It cracks open against high-volume mortal wound output or burst-damage lists that can delete full units in a single activation before the Command phase repair cycle kicks in.
518: Built around Lokhust Destroyers, Lokhust Lords, Skorpekh Destroyers, Skorpekh Lords, Ophydian Destroyers, Nekrosor Ammentar, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Lychguard, and the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon under Cursed Legion, this list weaponises the detachment's Strength escalation chain — once any Destroyer Cult unit kills or cripples an enemy, every Destroyer Cult weapon in the army climbs another two Strength for the rest of that turn, turning a good combat phase into a cascade of overkill. The plan is to deliver multiple simultaneous threats across the board, force opponents into no-win trade decisions, and let that kill-trigger snowball shred whatever survives contact. It punishes low-model elite armies that can't screen all angles at once, because the mobile toolkit means the Strength bonus activates reliably regardless of where the first kill lands. It struggles against durable horde builds or anything that can deny the initial kill-trigger, stalling the cascade before it starts and leaving the Destroyers hitting at base profile against a sea of bodies.
517: Built around near-universal Doomsday Arks, the Silent King, Technomancers, Canoptek Wraiths, Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers running the Starshatter Arsenal detachment, this list plays aggressive, mobile firepower anchored to objectives. The engine is simple and punishing: every ranged attack made within range of an objective marker gains +1 to hit, so the Doomsday Arks' heavy guns hit reliably from turn one while the Assault rule lets Vehicles shoot after moving without penalty, keeping the army fluid rather than static. It punishes gunline armies that cede board presence early, layering deep-striking Flayed Ones and Ophydian Destroyers to contest objectives and force the hit bonus online across the whole battlefield. Concentrated alpha-strike lists that can destroy the Arks before they fire, or high-mobility armies that deny objective proximity to the vehicles, bleed the hit bonus dry and expose how dependent the shooting platform is on that single condition.
530: Built around Allarus Custodians, Vertus Praetors, Dawneagle Shield-Captains, Allarus Shield-Captains, Witchseekers, Blade Champions, Custodian Guard, and Custodian Wardens, this is a spread-and-isolate mid-board brawler that deliberately keeps units apart to trigger its detachment's +1 to hit and wound whenever no friendly unit sits within 6". The win condition is dominating the midfield through elite melee threats operating as lone wolves — each unit fights at peak efficiency in isolation, making it extremely difficult for the opponent to prioritise targets without leaving others unchecked. It punishes low-model-count armies that can't flood the board with screens, because one-on-one the Custodes always win that trade. It cracks open when faced with dense horde lists or aggressive deep strike threats that can collapse the spacing discipline and stack friendlies together, stripping the hit-and-wound bonus at the worst possible moment.
525: Built around Land Speeder Vengeances, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, and a supporting core of Land Speeders, Ravenwing Black Knights, Outriders, and Ravenwing Command Squads, this list runs Company of Hunters and Darkflight Pursuit to create a fully mobile, cover-ignoring gunline. The plan is to Advance and shoot freely every turn — skimmers and bikes pour Assault firepower with Ignores Cover into whatever they want while Scout Squads hold backfield primaries and the mounted core contests the midboard. It absolutely punishes infantry-heavy lists and anything hiding in terrain, since Ignores Cover strips the defensive math those armies rely on. It cracks against elite armies that can weather the volume and close the gap fast, trading the board control back when the skimmer screen thins out.
529: Built around Wolf Guard Battle Leaders, Grey Hunters, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Wolf Scouts, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Ragnar Blackmane, Blood Claws, and Wolf Priests under Saga of the Beastslayer, this is a transport-heavy infantry swarm that floods the board with mobile, character-laden squads. The win condition is activating Lethal Hits army-wide by targeting Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles — letting even basic infantry units punch far above their weight against elite and armored targets — while Grey Hunters split and perform actions without surrendering their shooting. It punishes elite-heavy or monster-dense armies by stacking Lethal Hits across multiple concurrent threat vectors, making expensive single units cost-inefficient to protect. It struggles against mass-infantry hordes and gunlines that bypass its kill-chain entirely, leaving its Saga stalled and its mid-table brawlers exposed without the lethal-hits trigger firing.
521: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Ghostkeels, Pathfinders, Vespid Stingwings, Crisis Suits across all three loadouts, Riptides, Broadsides, Commander Farsight, and Coldstar Commanders, this is a full-spectrum T'au force blending hard-to-shift screening units with heavy mobile firepower across every slot. The plan is to use Pathfinders to Spot targets for Guided units, then unload massed battlesuit shooting — Sunforges and Starscythes for anti-armour, Fireknifes for mid-table pressure — while Stingwings and Kroot bodies contest objectives. It punishes heavy-armour lists badly, stacking mobile anti-tank across Riptides, Broadsides, and Crisis Suits to overload any list that relies on a small number of hard targets. It cracks under massed chaff or aggressive melee pressure that breaks its Pathfinder spotting network and forces battlesuits into sub-optimal ranges before their firepower can land.
441: Built around Librarians in Terminator Armour, Azrael, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and Sternguard Veterans operating under the Librarius Conclave, this list uses rotating Psychic Disciplines each battle round — cycling between Divination's re-roll aura and Biomancy's movement buff — to keep a dense terminator-and-elite infantry castle punching above its weight. The win condition is forcing opponents into its gun line while holding midfield with OC-boosted units under the Unforgiven Task Force's Command phase buff, screening with Scouts and Intercessors to deny deep-strike pressure into the core blob. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't flood objectives, where Sternguard massed fire and Companions' melee brutality systematically delete key units. Horde armies and high-mobility lists that bypass the castle's screen, contest multiple objectives simultaneously, and force it to spread thin crack it open entirely.
550: Built around multiple Lords of Change, Kairos Fateweaver, Be'lakor, and Screamers backed by Flamers, this list runs Lords of the Warp and Scintillating Legion together, stacking +1 Leadership and OC onto its non-monster Characters while banking Flux tokens to re-roll any single die at the critical moment across its Tzeentch units. The win condition is aggressive board saturation — fast-moving Lords of Change and Screamers race for midfield control and OC superiority while Flamers deliver layered lethal firepower, with Flux tokens converting near-misses into decisive kills or saves. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't contest multiple objectives simultaneously, overwhelming them through sheer mobile threat density and re-roll efficiency. It cracks open against armies that can reliably strip its Characters early, since losing OC and Leadership bonuses collapses the objective-hold engine the whole scoring plan depends on.
551: Built around Skarbrand, multiple Bloodthirsters, Rendmasters on Blood Throne, Bloodcrushers, Bloodletters, and Flesh Hounds flooding the board under Blood Legion, this is a wall-to-wall Khorne meat grinder supplemented by Nurgling and Plaguebearer screens. The win condition is reactive aggression — Blood Legion's surge move punishes every enemy advance by snapping Khorne units up to D6" closer mid-movement phase, letting the army compress space and force unfavorable charges on the opponent's turn while Warptide Bloodletter blobs advance and still charge. It punishes slower, armored melee lists and anything that needs to move into scoring positions, because the surge mechanism turns the opponent's own movement into fuel for getting killed. It cracks against armies that can park and shoot from range, since the horde has limited ranged threat and a single bad surge roll can leave the hardest-hitting pieces just out of charge range at the worst moment.
459: Built around Rogal Dorn Commanders, Scout Sentinels, Hellhounds, Leman Russ Battle Tanks, Leman Russ Vanquishers, Rogal Dorn Battle Tanks, and Tech-Priest Enginseers, this is a heavy armoured gunline running the Designation Force detachment, whose Signal Flares ability lets Scout Sentinels and Smoke infantry tag priority targets for the rest of the armoured column. The plan is to use Sentinels as forward spotters, paint high-value targets with Signal Flares, then erase them with concentrated Vanquisher and Dorn firepower while Hellhounds clear screening infantry to open up those kill lanes. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies that cannot hide expensive units behind screens, because Signal Flares forces engagement and the volume of high-AP tank weapons overwhelms tough single-wound targets. It cracks against aggressive swarm or mid-board pressure lists that can surround and lock down vehicles before they fire, exploiting the inherent immobility of a static gunline with limited melee threat.
465: Built around Daemonettes, Defilers, Lords Exultant, Infractors, Tormentors, Chaos Rhinos, and Noise Marines, this Carnival of Excess list is a mid-table brawling horde that keeps Emperor's Children and Legions of Excess units stacked within 6" of each other to maintain Empowered status and stack Sustained Hits across the entire force. The win condition is a coordinated wave assault — Rhino-mounted infantry crash into the midfield while Defilers provide mobile anti-armour punch, and the Lord Exultant with Possessed Blade amplifies the kill chain to grind opponents off objectives through sheer volume of sustained attacks. It punishes defensive gunlines and elite low-model-count armies that cannot absorb the Sustained Hits output from multiple Empowered units hitting simultaneously across several combat phases. Anything that can deny the 6" coherence bubble — mass screening, forced displacement, or alpha strikes that delete the anchor units before the engine activates — collapses the Empowered synergy and leaves individual units performing well below their threat ceiling.
546: Built around the Void Dragon, Nightbringer, one or more Transcendent C'tan, and the Deceiver, with Flayed Ones, Hexmark Destroyers, and Immortals rounding out the core under the Hand of the Dynasty detachment. The plan is to use the C'tan as durable, mobile damage dealers that contest and threaten midboard simultaneously, while Immortals advance and still perform actions thanks to Hand of the Dynasty's Assault-granting rule, keeping secondaries ticking even under pressure. It punishes lists that rely on volume light-to-medium firepower, since stacking multiple hard-bodied monsters forces opponents into anti-tank overload decisions they simply cannot win across all targets in one turn. However, coordinated high-AP multi-damage output or alpha-strike lists that can isolate and delete C'tan one at a time before they interact crack this build open, since losing one anchor unit per turn is a tempo hole the list cannot recover from.
544: Built around multiple Skorpekh Lords leading Skorpekh Destroyer squads, supported by Nekrosor Ammentar, Illuminor Szeras, the Void Dragon, the Silent King, and Lokhust Lords paired with Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, this is a mobile all-arms assault list running Awakened Dynasty, where every CHARACTER-led unit gains +1 to Hit on all attacks. The plan is to crash multiple buffed melee hammers into the opponent's key units while Lokhust Heavy Destroyers and the Void Dragon apply anti-armour overload from range, with Ophydian Destroyers and Necron Warriors locking down or contesting secondaries. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot handle simultaneous threats across multiple axes — the +1 Hit stacks lethal output across both melee and shooting, making trading inefficient for the opponent. It cracks when faced with aggressive alpha-strike lists or heavy screen denial that prevents the melee hammers from engaging on favorable terms before the Necron force is attrited below critical mass.
526: Built around Nekrosor Ammentar, multiple Lokhust Lord buffers, Lokhust Destroyers, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Lychguard, the Void Dragon, and an Overlord with Translocation Shroud, this is a high-mobility combined-arms machine with no fixed detachment identity. The win condition is threatening multiple vectors simultaneously — Ophydians tunneling into flanks, Destroyer units repositioning with Lokhust Lords to stack lethal firepower, and the Void Dragon cracking heavy armor while Lychguard hold or contest primary. It punishes mid-range gunlines and low-mobility armies that cannot respond to threats arriving from multiple angles in the same turn. It cracks open when faced with aggressive alpha-strike pressure or dense screening that collapses its repositioning corridors before the kill chains can assemble.

668: Built around multiple Lords of Change, Kairos Fateweaver, Screamers, Flamers, and Pink Horrors, this Tzeentch daemon force runs the Scintillating Legion detachment supported by Warptide in nearly nine out of ten lists, blending elite flying monsters with cheap mobile chaff into a fluid, toolbox-style force. The engine is Flux token re-rolls amplifying already-layered hit, wound, and damage output from Flamers and Lords of Change, while Warptide lets Battleline units advance-and-shoot or advance-then-charge to contest objectives without sacrificing offensive tempo. It punishes slower armies with durable elite backbones by drowning them in compounding re-roll efficiency and multi-vector threat angles that are near-impossible to prioritise against simultaneously. It cracks open against fast, high-volume anti-infantry shooting that exhausts Flux tokens early and strips the Pink Horror screen before the monster threats can close distance.
664: Built around Bloodcrushers, Beasts of Nurgle, Flesh Hounds, and a Rendmaster on Blood Throne alongside Be'lakor, a Bloodthirster, and a Great Unclean One, this is a Cavalcade of Chaos cavalry swarm that floods the board with fast, durable threats across both Khorne and Nurgle keywords. The engine is relentless fall-back-and-charge pressure — Cavalcade lets LEGIONES DAEMONICA MOUNTED units disengage without losing fight or shoot eligibility, letting Bloodcrushers and Flesh Hounds cycle combat continuously while Nurglings and Plaguebearers screen and hold primaries behind them. It punishes brawler lists and anything that relies on trading combat to neutralize threats, since the fall-back-and-charge loop means melee engagement never actually locks this army down. It cracks open against shooting-heavy alpha-strike lists that can strip the cavalry before the loop activates, and elite low-drop armies that win initiative and delete key pieces before the layered lethality comes online.
665: Built around Plaguebearers, Nurglings, Beasts of Nurgle, Bloodletters, a Bloodthirster, and Be'lakor, this is a mass-horde army running Shadow Legion that floods the board with layered Nurgle bodies backed by hard-hitting Khorne elements. The Warptide detachment lets Battleline units advance and still shoot and charge, so Plaguebearers and Bloodletters push up aggressively each turn — threatening objectives while Be'lakor and the Bloodthirster hunt priority targets in the mid-table brawl. It punishes slow, static armies that can't clear volume: stacking wounds across three or more waves of bodies with lethal keyword saturation bleeds opponents dry on resources and actions. It cracks open against elite armies with efficient, high-AP shooting that can strip hordes faster than the list regenerates board presence, particularly if Be'lakor is neutralised early and the threat sequencing collapses.
653: Built around Vashtorr, multiple Defilers, Venomcrawlers, and Warpsmiths supported by Cultist screens, this is a Soulforged Warpack list that turns its Daemon Vehicles into a rolling armoured tide by leveraging Dark Pacts to add 1 to Wound rolls and +2 Attacks in melee simultaneously. The plan is to keep Vashtorr and the Warpsmiths buffing and repairing the vehicle pack while Cultists hold backfield objectives, freeing the Defilers and Venomcrawlers to bully midboard and crack armour with boosted Dark Pact outputs. It punishes mechanised and heavily armoured lists badly, stacking mobile anti-armour threats that are individually hard to trade into efficiently. Dedicated mass high-AP shooting or alpha-strike lists that can kill vehicles before Dark Pacts fire will gut the engine before it gets going.
647: Built around twin Defilers, waves of Cultist Mobs, Chosen, Abaddon the Despoiler, Huron Blackheart, Masters of the Maelstrom, and Red Corsairs Raiders, this Pactbound Zealots list operates as a grinding mass-horde gunline that can also threaten armour across the table. The Pactbound Zealots detachment grants Lethal Hits on unmodified 5+ melee rolls, so Chosen and Abaddon's combat threats become genuinely punishing the moment the horde screen clears a path — scoring flows from holding mid-table while the Defilers apply persistent anti-armour and suppression pressure. It punishes opponent lists that rely on elite infantry or light vehicles by drowning them in volume attacks that constantly fish for Critical Hits. It cracks open against armies that can efficiently clear the cultist screen at range before the melee engine closes, leaving Abaddon and Chosen exposed without the bodies to protect them.
470: Built around a swarm of War Dog Karnivores, Brigands, Executioners, and Stalkers screened by Cultist Mobs, this is a pure War Dog flood list running Houndpack Lance. The win condition is simple brutality: every Command phase, one enemy unit is marked and every War Dog attacking it gains Sustained Hits 1, funneling that concentrated firepower and melee into erasing a high-value target per turn while the rest of the pack clears chaff and contests objectives. It punishes armour-heavy lists mercilessly, delivering layered anti-tank output from multiple angles that few mechanised forces can absorb across multiple rounds. Its weakness is elite infantry or screening armies that can isolate and mob individual War Dogs in melee, where the pack's relatively low model-count flanks get picked apart before the Sustained Hits mark can do its work.
649: Built around Huron Blackheart, Abaddon the Despoiler, two squads of Chosen, Possessed, a Defiler, Red Corsairs Raiders, and a Cultist Mob screening the whole enterprise, this is a mass-horde midfield brawler running either Creations of Bile or Huron's Marauders depending on the pilot. The plan is to flood the board with bodies through Masters of the Maelstrom, use the Cultist screen to protect priority threats, then crash Abaddon and Chosen into whatever is holding objectives while Huron's command-phase ability chains buffs across visible Heretic Astartes Infantry. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't clear chaff fast enough before the melee hammer arrives. Armies with strong shooting that can strip the screen early, or anything that can isolate Abaddon before he engages, will collapse the kill chain before it lands.
635: Built around Land Speeder Vengeancess, standard Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, and Deathwing Knights, with Azrael and Inner Circle Companions rounding out the core, all running the Darkflight Pursuit detachment to give every RAVENWING FLY unit Ignores Cover on ranged attacks. It struggles against armies that can alpha strike the fragile speeder chassis before they fire, or that field enough durable, high-OC bodies to out-hold objectives that the Knights and infantry core cannot contest fast enough.
652: Built around a pair of Defilers and Venomcrawlers as the heavy engine, supported by Abaddon the Despoiler, Kravek Morne, and a deep screen of Cultist Mobs, Nurglings, and Beasts of Nurgle, all operating under Pactbound Zealots — a detachment that grants Lethal Hits on unmodified melee 5+ rolls to its units. The plan is to use Red Corsairs Raiders and screening chaff to contest the mid-board while the Defilers and Venomcrawlers project anti-armour firepower from range, with Abaddon threatening to crack anything that gets too close and the Lethal Hits engine accelerating melee kill speed across the roster. It punishes mechanised and armour-heavy lists hard, combining long-range anti-tank output with melee pressure that makes parking vehicles near objectives genuinely dangerous. It cracks open when faced with aggressive alpha-strike armies that can isolate and remove the Defilers early, since the screening layer — while wide — lacks the durability to absorb a full-force trade in the first two turns.
638: Built around Ravenwing Black Knights, Ravenwing Command Squads, Outrider Squads, Sammael, Lion El'Jonson, Azrael, and Chaplain on Bike, this is a high-speed Dark Angels cavalry force that floods the midboard with hard-hitting bike units backed by Scout screens and Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes. The plan is to project threat from turn one — bikes surge into scoring positions while Sammael, Azrael, and the Lion stack auras to punch well above their weight in melee and shooting, converting mobility into both kills and objective control. It punishes slower gunlines and elite infantry that can't reposition to contest, drowning them in fast-moving bodies across multiple angles simultaneously. Anything with reliable blast-heavy area denial, mass high-AP shooting, or strong counter-charge units in the midfield can blunt the cavalry wave before it converts momentum into a score lead.
640: Built around Librarians in Terminator Armour, Inner Circle Companions, Deathwing Knights, and Azrael, this is a psyker-amplified elite infantry list running the Inner Circle Task Force and Librarius Conclave to stack psychic disciplines across every unit simultaneously. The win condition is controlling the Vowed objective swing — flexing between Defensive Footing to lock down a held marker and Aggressive Push to contest multiple enemy objectives at once — while Divination Discipline's hit and wound re-rolls pump out reliable elite-unit firepower through Sternguard and Companions. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that can't contest multiple objectives simultaneously, leveraging the transport-heavy infantry core to reposition Terminators and Companions into scoring positions faster than opponents expect. Mass mortal wounds, volume anti-infantry shooting, and anything that strips the Librarian buffs before combat collapses the entire psychic engine the list depends on.
451: Built around Lady Malys, Drazhar, Archons, Incubi in Venoms, Wyches, Ravagers, Mandrakes, and Scourges, this list blends Exhibition Of Slaughter's Lethal Hits on Wych Cult melee with Skysplinter Assault's Lance and Ignores Cover on disembarking units to stack brutal close-range burst damage across a wide horde footprint. The gameplan is to flood the midboard with cheap bodies screening priority pieces, then surge transports forward so disembarking Incubi and Wyches hit with Lance melee while Ravagers and Scourges erase targets that try to hold distance. It punishes armies that rely on light-to-medium infantry blocks and cover-dependent fire positions, overwhelming them with layered lethal melee and flat-ignoring their terrain advantages. However, anything that can crack the fragile Venoms before the assault lands — high-volume anti-transport shooting or alpha-strike melee — collapses the entire delivery mechanism and leaves the infantry stranded mid-table.
596: Built around Librarians, Deathwatch Veterans, Terminator Squads, Indomitor Kill Teams, and Sternguard Veterans running Bastion Task Force with Librarius Conclave support, this is a heavily armed infantry gunline that keeps moving without sacrificing firepower — Battleline units shoot and act freely after Advancing or Falling Back, and Librarius Conclave cycles psychic disciplines each round to layer re-rolls, extra movement, or bonus damage on the right unit at the right moment. The win condition is sustained mid-table fire superiority: transport the kill packages forward, pick the correct discipline, and grind the opponent's scoring pieces off objectives through sheer volume of accurate, specialist-ammunition shooting. It punishes slow, high-wound armies that can't clear entrenched infantry efficiently, exploiting the build's ability to Advance onto objectives while still firing and performing actions. However, hard alpha-strike lists that delete transports and key Librarians early — stripping the discipline engine and stranding infantry — can collapse the tempo the entire plan depends on.
654: Built around Lady Malys, Incubi, Drazhar, Wyches, Reavers, Scourges, and a swarm of Venoms, this list runs Skysplinter Assault alongside Exhibition Of Slaughter to create a layered disembark-and-murder engine across a massive horde of bodies. The plan is to flood the midboard with transports, disembark into threat range, and let Skysplinter's Ignores Cover on ranged weapons and Lance on melee weapons — combined with Exhibition's Lethal Hits on all Wych Cult melee attacks against non-Monsters and non-Vehicles — convert volume into catastrophic kill turns that bury opponents in VP. It punishes defensive, screen-heavy armies brutally, since the sheer number of disembarking units with stacked combat buffs overwhelms any attempt to castle or deny space. It cracks open against elite anti-tank overload lists that can strip Venoms before they deliver their passengers, collapsing the entire disembark engine in one surgical alpha strike.
672:
Built around multiple squads of Infractors delivered in Chaos Rhinos, Lord Exultants buffing them into melee, Tormentors and winged Daemon Princes pressuring flanks, Defilers providing heavy fire support, and Noise Marines holding ground, this is a transport-infantry swarm running Coterie of the Conceited.

The engine is Pact point generation through the pledge mechanic — you commit to a kill count each battle round, then crash Rhino-born Infractors and Daemon Princes into enemy lines to hit that number, converting successful pledges into escalating power across the game.

It punishes mid-density infantry armies brutally, with multiple fast melee threats arriving simultaneously to overwhelm screens and rack up the kills needed to meet pledges.

Where it cracks is against elite or durable lists that deny the kill count — if pledges go unmet, the Pact engine stalls, and without that fuel the army loses its late-game teeth.
675: Built around Infractors, Lords Exultant, Tormentors, Noise Marines, and Flawless Blades riding in Chaos Rhinos, supported by Chaos Spawn screens, Defilers, and Daemon Princes of Slaanesh with Wings, this is an infantry-heavy mid-table brawler that floods the board with transported assault elements. The engine is a charge-and-fight cascade: units pile out of Rhinos to trigger charge-dependent detachment bonuses — whether that's Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1 from Peerless Bladesmen, Fights First from Spectacle of Slaughter on Flawless Blades, or Slaanesh Pact point accumulation through Coterie of the Conceited — converting melee volume into scoring pressure and attrition. It punishes static gunlines and slow defensive builds that cannot peel overlapping threats off multiple objectives simultaneously. It cracks against mobile elite armies that can avoid engagement, kite the Rhino deliveries, or anti-tank overload the transports before the infantry ever disembark.
436: Built around Myphitic Blight-Haulers, Foetid Bloat-Drones (both variants), Poxwalkers, Deathshroud Terminators, and Lords of Contagion and Virulence, this list runs the Contagion Engines detachment to give all its daemon engines ASSAULT on their ranged weapons, turning advance-and-shoot into a full-pressure threat across the whole board. The plan is to flood objectives with Poxwalker screens while the daemon engines push up freely, stacking Contagion Range infections and layering mortal wounds through Death Lord's Chosen's Afflicted-unit triggers each Command phase. This punishes static, low-model-count armies that can't clear the screen without exposing themselves to the daemon engine kill chain, and rewards early Contagion application snowballing into unavoidable attrition. However, high-mobility lists that can outrange the advance or alpha-strike the daemon engines before Contagion spreads will gut the engine before the layered lethality activates.
633: Built around Achilles Ridgerunners, Neophyte Hybrids, Purestrain Genestealers, Patriarch, Benefictus, Hyperadapted Raveners, Deathleaper, Acolyte Hybrids, Atalan Jackals, and The Red Terror, this Final Day list floods the board with both Cult bodies and Tyranids Vanguard Invader allies, blending a horde of cheap screens with multiple elite melee threats across every wave. The win condition is attrition through volume — Neophytes heal three wounds per Command phase while holding terrain, Purestrain Genestealers and Raveners punch into combat repeatedly, and the Patriarch with Inhuman Integration and Enraptured Damnation keeps the kill chain alive deep into late turns. It punishes low-model armies through sheer wound saturation, making prioritisation nearly impossible when cheap Acolytes and Jackals contest objectives while Genestealers threaten flanks. Heavy blast weapons and board-wide mortal wound output crack it open, deleting entire horde units before the melee engine can reach its targets.
688: Built around multiple Nemesis Dreadknights, Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Strike Squads, and Interceptor Squads, this list is a mobile heavy-metal hammer that floods the board with Dreadknight-class threats across detachments ranging from Immaterial Interdiction to Brotherhood Strike. The win condition is overwhelming the opponent's anti-tank budget simultaneously — multiple Grand Masters and standard Dreadknights advance aggressively, forcing the opponent to either cede midboard control or split fire inefficiently while Interceptor Squads use surge moves to contest secondaries. It punishes lists that rely on a narrow anti-armour threat concentration, as simply removing one or two Dreadknights leaves the rest free to dominate close-range scoring. Armies packing dense, cheap screening units or elite multi-damage infantry can neutralise the Dreadknights' mobility advantage by denying clean charge lanes and bleeding efficiency from the list's relatively small model count.
634: Built around Achilles Ridgerunners, Reductus Saboteurs, Purestrain Genestealers, Acolyte Hybrids, Neophyte Hybrids, Atalan Jackals, Benefictus, and Goliath Rockgrinders, this is a dense horde-gunline hybrid that layers ranged firepower from Ridgerunners over a wall of cheap bodies. The win condition is objective stranglehold through volume — Outlander Claw keeps Atalan Jackals locking down controlled markers while Neophytes heal inside terrain under Xenocult Masses, and Purestrains threaten to escape combat and reposition via Purestrain Broodswarm's strategic reserve exit. It punishes low-model-count lists by overwhelming their screening and anti-horde capacity simultaneously across multiple threat vectors. Heavy anti-tank alpha strikes and elite melee units that can delete the Ridgerunners early crack this open, since the mobile firepower anchor is hard to replace mid-game.
689: Built around multiple Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Purgation Squads, Castellan Crowe leading Purifiers, Strike Squads, and Brotherhood Terminators, this is a Brotherhood Strike list that drops the bulk of its combat power from deep strike with re-rolled hits and wounds on arrival. The engine is a coordinated deep strike wave: Purgation Squads pin key enemy units and force battle-shock rolls at -1 through Fires of Purgation, softening priority targets while Dreadknights and Purifiers crash in to finish them, all backed by the Tome of Forbidden Ways to extend threat range and flexibility. It punishes static or low-mobility armies that can't avoid the drop zones, overwhelming them with simultaneous multi-angle pressure that tight positioning alone can't answer. Armies that can bubble-wrap effectively, deny landing zones, or generate enough bodies to absorb the initial wave will bleed this list dry, since it has limited capacity to grind through a sustained attrition fight once the deep strike window closes.
615: Built around Berehk Stornbröw, Einhyr Hearthguard, Cthonian Beserks, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and a mobile core of Sagitaurs and Hekaton Land Fortresses, this list runs Hearthguard Covenant to squeeze re-rolls on wound rolls of 1 for its elite close-range fighters, then leans on either Needgaârd or Mercenary Oathband as a secondary YP engine. The plan is to crash up the board mid-table, generating YP from kills while Thunderkyn and Sagitaurs hammer from range and Beserks threaten brutal close-quarters engagements. It punishes slow or static gunlines that cannot prevent the mid-table collision — once the Hearthguard and Beserks are in the opponent's face at under 9", the wound re-rolls make every volley hurt disproportionately. Highly mobile, elite armies that can screen effectively and dictate engagement range deny the close-range wound re-roll synergy and bleed this list dry in the mid-game.
700: Built around the Cerastus Knight Lancer — fast, hard-hitting close-combat cavalry filling multiple slots — this list runs the Questoris Companions detachment, stacking Oaths turn over turn to layer escalating bonuses across an already aggressive chassis. The engine is momentum: fulfill one Oath, immediately gain another, keeping every Knight buffed with compounding objectives as the army closes distance and strips armor with mobile anti-tank pressure from multiple angles simultaneously. It punishes lists that rely on a single durable threat or slow defensive lines, since the multi-Knight frontage forces impossible priority choices while the Lancer's mobility denies safe backfield positioning. Concentrated high-AP firepower or massed elite melee that can match the Lancer's threat range cracks this list open — if the Oath chain is interrupted by attrition before it compounds, the army loses its engine.
621: Built around multiple Hekaton Land Fortresses, Hernkyn Pioneers, Kapricus Carriers, and Einhyr Hearthguard — supported by Hernkyn Yaegirs, Arkanyst Evaluators, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and a deep bench of infantry — this is a grinding midboard brawler that floods the table with bodies and armour simultaneously. The win condition is attrition: the Hekatons anchor fire corridors while massed infantry swarms objectives, with Arkanyst Evaluators and Memnyr Strategists coordinating overlapping shooting lanes to grind opponents off the midboard turn by turn. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't trade efficiently against the sheer volume of units and the durability of multiple heavy vehicles. It struggles against fast alpha-strike lists that can isolate and crack individual Hekatons before the firebase concentrates, unravelling the whole structure.
617: Built around Hernkyn Pioneers, Kapricus Carriers, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Cthonian Beserks, Hekaton Land Fortresses, Einhyr Hearthguard, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and Hearthkyn Warriors under the Farseekers detachment, this is a fast, layered mid-board brawler that floods the table with bikes, skimmers, and infantry. The Farseekers' +1 to hit for Hernkyn units within 12" rewards aggressive positioning, letting Pioneers and Yaegirs reliably crack targets while Beserks and Hearthguard crash into whatever survives the shooting phase. It punishes slow, durable gunlines that can't contest the mid-board, smothering them under layered lethal firepower from Thunderkyn and Land Fortresses before closing with melee threats. Armies that can thin the screen fast or alpha-strike the bike elements before they get into the 12" sweet spot disrupt the hit-bonus engine the entire list depends on.
620: Built around Hernkyn Pioneers, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and Kapricus Carriers, this is a mechanized mid-board brawler that floods the table with fast-moving Hernkyn units exploiting the detachment's +1 to hit within 12" to turn short-range firepower into a precision killbox. The plan is to advance rapidly, collapse the midfield, and compound early kills through the secondary Oathband rule that banks YP each time an enemy unit is destroyed, fueling board-wide pressure. This army punishes aggressive infantry-heavy lists that walk into the 12" kill window, where layered Thunderkyn and Steeljack volleys become brutally efficient. It cracks open against elite, long-range shooting armies that can strip the vehicle screens before the Hernkyn units ever close to effective range.
619: Built around Ûthar the Destined, Einhyr Hearthguard, Kâhls, Hekaton Land Fortresses, Sagitaurs, and Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, this is a mid-board brawler wrapped in a heavy gunline shell — elite infantry delivered by transports and supported by layered long-range firepower. The Hearthguard Covenant's wound-roll-of-1 rerolls within 9" rewards aggressive positioning, so the plan is to crash Hearthguard and Ûthar into the enemy's face at close range while Thunderkyn and Land Fortresses punish anything that tries to respond from distance. It shreds opposing lists that rely on moderate-toughness, low-save units — anything that can't shrug repeated high-volume, high-strength shooting and melee combined arms gets dismantled piecemeal. Armies that can screen the 9" bubble effectively or deliver a concentrated alpha strike before the Hearthguard close crack it open, since the build's payoff mechanics demand it gets there intact.
616: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Cthonian Beserks, and Hekaton Land Fortresses, this is a dense mid-table brawler that floods the board with durable infantry and hard-hitting vehicles under the Hearthband detachment. The engine is close-range attrition: Hearthguard and Beserks push into Engagement Range to trigger Hearthband's re-roll-wound-1 and AP improvement on Hearthguard, while Thunderkyn and Land Fortresses pour fire into whatever the melee wave pins down. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot trade efficiently into multiple waves of tough bodies, grinding through their key pieces faster than they can respond. It cracks open against highly mobile screens and alpha-strike lists that can isolate and delete the Hearthguard before they close distance, stripping the list's primary damage spike before it activates.
618: Built around Cthonian Beserks, Sagitaurs, Hearthkyn Warriors, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Hernkyn Pioneers, Hekaton Land Fortresses, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and supporting characters, this is a mechanised mid-board brawler that uses Scouts 6" on every Sagitaur to surge infantry-packed transports into scoring range before the game truly begins. The core plan is to flood mid-table with massed transported infantry while Brôkhyr Thunderkyn and Hekaton Land Fortresses suppress or destroy armoured threats, creating a layered wave that is perpetually contesting primaries. It punishes slow, static gunlines that cannot shift an entrenched, multi-wave mechanised advance before the attrition math tips irrecoverably. Tight screen-and-deny armies and fast alpha-strike lists that can strip transports before deployment ends expose how dependent the build is on delivering its infantry cargo intact.
623:
The faction label says Leagues of Votann but every unit, detachment, and enhancement in the evidence is unambiguously Space Marines — specifically a Raven Guard or Vanguard-flavored Adeptus Astartes roster. Built around a Lieutenant with combi-weapon, Intercessor Squads, and a Librarian cycling Psychic Disciplines each battle round, this list blends a resilient midfield infantry core with a mobile, pressure-oriented support structure.

The plan is to project ranged threat from a durable gunline — amplified by the Librarian's rotating disciplines granting hit and wound re-rolls or movement buffs — while the Lieutenant anchors scoring and the infantry holds ground under a cover bubble that activates against attacks from beyond 12 inches.

It punishes attrition-focused lists that rely on slowly grinding through infantry, because the cover mechanic and discipline flexibility make the core surprisingly hard to trade into efficiently.

It cracks open against aggressive close-range assault armies or heavy alpha-strike lists that can close inside 12 inches quickly, neutralizing the cover benefit and overwhelming the relatively light melee output of the core units before the disciplines can compensate.
535: Built around Scout Squads, Sternguard Veterans, Librarians, and Intercessors, this is a Space Marines force that mixes early board presence with a heavy gunline backbone — Ballistus Dreadnoughts and Gladiator Lancers supplying ranged anti-armour while infantry flood forward zones. The plan is to lock down objectives early with Scouts and Intercessors, then grind out scoring through durable, well-positioned infantry while the Librarian cycles Psychic Disciplines to amplify hit/wound output or push movement where needed. It punishes slower, lower-model-count armies that can't contest the midboard, using transport-delivered Sternguard to threaten precise, high-AP volleys into exposed elite infantry. It struggles against fast aggressive armies that can crack the gunline before it sets — anything that forces it off objectives early collapses its scoring engine.
455: Built around Skorpekh Lords, Skorpekh Destroyers, Nekrosor Ammentar, and C'tan Shards of the Nightbringer and Void Dragon, this list runs Cursed Legion to stack +2 Strength onto its Destroyer Cult weapons — and chains a second +2 onto any unit that destroys or halves an enemy in the same turn, turning each kill into a snowballing threat. The plan is to crash melee-heavy Destroyer Cult units and C'tan into the opponent's frontline early, using Ophydian Destroyers' natural deep strike access and Skyshroud Spearhead's Tomb Blades deep strike to threaten from multiple angles simultaneously and force no-win positioning decisions. It punishes static or low-mobility armies that can't peel multiple simultaneous threats, as the stacked Strength bonuses let Destroyer Cult mulch high-toughness units that would otherwise wall them. It cracks under pressure from armies that can alpha-strike the Destroyer Cult before the kill-chain triggers, since the Strength engine requires landing the first kill to fully come online.
659: Built around the Void Dragon, the Nightbringer, the Deceiver, up to two Transcendent C'tan, Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers, this list floods the table with independent god-tier threats that each demand a dedicated answer. The win condition is threat saturation — the opponent simply cannot kill every C'tan before they make contact, and whichever god-shard survives advances to delete priority targets while Flayed Ones and Ophydian Destroyers burst from deep strike or infiltration to contest and punish backfield units. It punishes elite-but-low-model-count armies viciously, because every activation an opponent spends unsuccessfully grinding through a C'tan's wound pool is another activation where Ophydians are already at their throat. Armies that can generate massed high-volume, multi-damage output across several units simultaneously crack this list open by forcing it to trade gods for bodies, since once the C'tan start dying the layered lethality collapses faster than the objective presence can compensate.
658: Built around the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer, C'tan Shard of the Deceiver, Transcendent C'tan, and Imotekh the Stormlord under the Pantheon of Woe detachment, this is a wall of Necrons Monsters flooding the board with Distortion Fields auras. The win condition is suffocating enemy armor saves across a wide frontage — every enemy unit within 6" of a C'tan is unravelling, shredding AP across the entire army's output while the monsters grind through anything they touch. It brutally punishes mid-range gunlines and elite infantry dependent on strong saves, since multiple overlapping Distortion Fields mean virtually no attack in the game fires at its printed AP. Highly mobile armies that can consistently avoid the 6" aura bubbles, or volume-fire hordes that don't care about AP degradation, can chip the C'tan down before the attrition engine overwhelms them.
569: Built around the Defiler — a hulking Chaos engine that combines ranged firepower with melee threat — this list floods the board with a flexible toolkit of daemon engines, infantry screens, and support characters drawn from a rotating cast of minority picks. The core plan is to use the Defiler's dual-threat profile to contest midfield objectives while layering supplementary pressure from whatever supporting cast the pilot has assembled, denying the opponent clean answers by spreading threats across multiple vectors. It punishes lists that rely on a single removal priority, since eliminating the Defiler still leaves mobile infantry and daemon support intact to grind out secondaries. It cracks apart when faced with high-volume, high-AP shooting that can strip the Defiler's wounds efficiently and collapse the toolkit before it spreads damage, leaving the variable supporting pieces too isolated to recover.
622: Built around Vertus Praetors, Allarus Custodians, and a Shield-Captain on Dawneagle Jetbike, this is a fast, elite Adeptus Custodes force that leverages high-mobility golden warriors to contest and hold objectives across the mid-table. The engine is aggressive jetbike pressure — Vertus Praetors and the mounted Shield-Captain project threat early while Allarus Custodians hit flanks or drop zones to punish exposed targets, with variable Knight support adding anti-armour overload against heavier builds. It punishes low-volume, high-quality armies that can't generate enough attacks to grind through elite statlines and layered saves. Armies with efficient, high-volume mortal wound output or mass AP-2/3 shooting can strip the elite units faster than the list can score decisive board control.
603: Built around Gretchin screens, Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Lootas, Flash Gitz, Tankbustas, and Ghazghkull Thraka leading a core of Boyz, this is a horde army that layers cheap bodies in front of serious ranged firepower. The plan is to use Gretchin and Boyz as a disposable screen and objective-sitters while the gunline — Lootas, Flash Gitz, and Shokk Attack Guns — grinds opponents down at range, with Ghazghkull enabling the Waaagh! to turbocharge infantry shooting across the board. It punishes slow, static armies that can't clear through multiple waves of chaff before the ranged units find their targets. It cracks open against fast, aggressive lists that can bypass the screen early or alpha-strike the fragile shooters before Painboy support and Zodgrod's grots can absorb enough punishment.
702: Built around Flash Gitz, Ghazghkull Thraka, Boyz, Nobz, Breaka Boyz, Bannernobs, and Warbosses hauled forward in Trukks and Battlewagons, this is a Freebooter Krew horde that floods the midboard with bodies and guns simultaneously. 677:
Built around multiple Librarians buffing Intercessors, Scout Squads, and Bladeguard Veterans, this list fields a broad infantry force with psychic discipline cycling — rotating between Biomancy, Divination, and Pyromancy to suit the round's demands — while pushing bodies into heavy gunline and transport-infantry postures across the board.

678: Built around Marneus Calgar, Captain Titus, Scout Squads, Wardens of Ultramar, and Bladeguard Veterans, this is a Reclamation Force list that plants its elite melee infantry on objectives and dares opponents to shift them. 686: Built around Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes, Scout Squads, and Intercessor Squads, this list leans hard into the Fulguris Task Force's first-turn ingress move to drop its entire Speeder battlegroup into aggressive mid-board positions before the opponent can react. 681: Built around a core of Librarians (including a Terminator-armoured variant), Sternguard Veterans, Bladeguard Veterans, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, and screening infantry in Scouts and Intercessors, the Librarius Conclave cycles its Psychic Disciplines each battle round to reshape how every Psyker unit on the table performs — toggling between Divination's re-rolls, Biomancy's movement boost, or Pyromancy's ranged threat to match the moment. 679: Built around Intercessor Squads, Scout Squads, and Repulsor Executioners, the Ceramite Sentinels detachment rewards holding terrain features by granting re-rolls to hit and wound of 1, plus the Entrenched keyword to any unit that occupies a terrain piece and didn't arrive from reserve that turn. 695: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators (typically two squads), Logan Grimnar, Arjac Rockfist, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Ragnar Blackmane, and Blood Claws under the Saga of the Great Wolf detachment, this is a dense, multi-threat infantry brawler with rotating Hunting Pack buffs cycling through the army each turn. 680: Built around Caanok Var, multiple Terminator Assault Squads, Sternguard Veterans, and a pair of Librarians supported by an Ancient in Terminator Armour, this list uses the Hammer of Avernii detachment's re-roll wounded rolls of 1 on the Oath of Moment target — and crucially, Caanok Var's RECALCULATING ability to immediately reassign Oath of Moment to a new target the moment the first dies, keeping that pressure chain running all game. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that field a tight hierarchy of key pieces, since chaining Oath reassignments means every turn a different cornerstone unit gets overloaded with re-rolls and volume fire. However, it struggles against wide hordes or split-threat lists that spread activations thin, because Oath of Moment only targets one unit at a time and the assault Terminators lack the volume or board reach to simultaneously suppress multiple objective-flooding threats.
676: Built around Infernus Squads, Bladeguard Veterans, Librarians, and a Land Raider Redeemer, this list weaponizes the Firestorm Assault Force detachment's core rule — every Adeptus Astartes ranged weapon gains Assault, and attacks within 12" gain +1 Strength — to transform close-range shooting into a punishing advance-and-fire engine. The plan is to push the Redeemer up the board, unload Infernus and Bladeguard at point-blank range, and stack Librarius Conclave's Divination or Pyromancy disciplines to amplify the short-range kill spike while Intercessors hold ground. 682: Built around Darnath Lysander, Terminator Assault Squads, Terminator Squads, Vanguard Veterans with jump packs, Bladeguard Veterans, and a Librarian, this list runs the Emperor's Shield detachment to generate full wound re-rolls on the Oath of Moment target via Lysander's personal aura, turning elite infantry into a relentless kill-focused engine. 528: Built around Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Arjac Rockfist, and Wolf Guard Battle Leaders backed by multiple Grey Hunters squads, this is a transport-heavy infantry surge running Saga of the Great Wolf. 614: Built around Commander Farsight, multiple Crisis suit variants (Starscythe, Sunforge, Fireknife), Coldstar and Enforcer Commanders, Stealth Battlesuits, the Twin Lance, Riptide, and Ghostkeel, this is a wall-to-wall battlesuit army running the Retaliation Cadre detachment. 599: Built around Broodlords, Genestealers, Neurolictors, Lictors, Biovores, Von Ryan's Leapers, Hyperadapted Raveners, Raveners, a Neurotyrant, Deathleaper, Zoanthropes, and Hormagaunts across the Ambush Predators and Vanguard Onslaught detachments, this is a deep-striking infiltration swarm that floods the table with independent threats arriving from every angle. 515: Built around biovores, maleceptors, exocrines, tyrannofexes, a hive tyrant, neurotyrant, norn emissary, genestealers, hormagaunts, and lictors, Invasion Fleet fields a deeply layered swarm that blends heavy synapse-fuelled shooting with aggressive melee threats across every phase. 723: Built around Sydonian Dragoons with taser lances, Ironstrider Ballistarii, Skitarii Rangers, Sicarian Infiltrators, Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, and Onager Dunecrawlers, this is a layered skimmer-fire gunline that hides its infantry inside a screen of fast cavalry. 492: Built around Allarus Custodians and a Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour backed by Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, Blade Champion, Witchseekers, Venatari Custodians, and Caladius Grav-Tanks, this list runs Shield Host as its primary detachment with Tharanatoi Hammerblow layered on top to let deep-striking Terminators re-roll charge rolls after an ingress move, creating a credible threat of turn-one contact. 736: Built around Windriders in mass, Warlock Skyrunners, War Walkers, Shroud Runners, Rangers, Shining Spears, and psyker support from Eldrad Ulthran and Farseer Skyrunners, this is a mobile Asuryani bike swarm that deploys the Windrider Host detachment's reserve trick to flood the board in waves, treating the battle round as one higher when bringing Mounted and Vyper units in from Strategic Reserves. 733: Built around Eldrad Ulthran, multiple Warlock Conclaves, Warlock Skyrunners, Warlocks, Farseers, Howling Banshees anchored by Jain Zar, Fire Dragons paired with Fuegan, War Walkers, Dark Reapers, and Storm Guardian screens, this is a Seer Council list that generates a pool of Fate dice at the start of the game and spends matching values to fuel its Stratagems for free. 439: Built around Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, Hastarii Fusiliers packed into Skorpius Duneriders, Sicarian Infiltrators, and layered Tech-Priest support from Skitarii Marshals and Tech-Priest Manipuli, this list runs a mobile firebase across all three detachment flavours — most commonly Lords of the Forge, which grants Tech-Priests a 4+/5+ FNP stack and the Baffling Data Screed debuff to strip Vehicle actions mid-game. 741: Built around Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Scout Sentinels, Gaunt's Ghosts, Cadian Shock Troops, Cadian Command Squads, Krieg Combat Engineers, and Kasrkin, this is a deep-bench elite infantry swarm that layers screening bodies over high-quality special weapons. 644: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Captains with Jump Packs, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, and cheap Scout and Intercessor screens, this is a jump-infantry swarm that floods the board with airborne threats across multiple threat vectors. The build punishes slow, defensive gunlines that cannot deal with simultaneous multi-flank pressure from high-mobility infantry arriving in waves. 446: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with jump packs, Assault Intercessors with jump packs, Commander Dante, Lemartes, Sanguinary Priests, and Bladeguard Veterans, this is a Liberator Assault Group list that weaponizes the detachment's charge bonus — +2 Strength and +1 Attack on every melee weapon after a charge — across multiple elite jump infantry threats simultaneously. It punishes slower gunline armies that cannot screen every angle, as jump infantry bypass positional defenses and the charge bonuses make even mid-tier units hit well above their points cost. 461: Built around waves of Plaguebearers, Beasts of Nurgle, Nurglings, and Great Unclean Ones supported by Rotigus, Sloppity Bilepipers, Poxbringers, and Epidemius, this is a Plague Legion list that floods the midboard with durable, layered bodies. Dense, overlapping screens and high-volume mortal wound output crack it open — anything that keeps daemonettes off objectives or tags and pins fiends before they can chain-charge collapses the tempo engine.
747: Built around War Dog Stalkers, Karnivores, and Brigands — a swarm of eight-plus medium Knights flooding the board with fast, hard-hitting chassis. This list punishes armies built around a few elite, expensive units — multiple independently threatening War Dogs force impossible target priority decisions, and no single removal piece can swing the game. It struggles against anything that can systematically strip War Dogs at range before they close, since the list carries no durability tech beyond weight of wounds and has no dedicated screen to absorb shooting lanes.
750: Built around Cultist Mobs flooding objectives, the Knight Abominant, Chaos Cerastus Knight Lancer, and Knight Despoiler, this Iconoclast Fiefdom list pairs cheap DAMNED infantry screens with multiple titanic threats. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear cheap screening units while simultaneously answering multiple heavy threats. Spread-thin lists that rely on concentrated anti-tank firepower to neutralise walkers will crack it, since the horde screen buys the Knights time — but high-volume mortal wound output or redundant anti-armour saturation can overwhelm the Knights before the infantry density pays off.
727: Built around Chaos Terminator Squads, Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Mutilators, Kravek Morne, and Cultist Mobs screened by Defilers, this is a Cabal of Chaos list that weaponises Dark Pacts to buff Psyker shooting and Daemon Prince combat, with the Warpstrike Champions detachment repositioning Terminators and Mutilators off the board at the end of the opponent's turn to threaten new angles each round.
