It punishes slower gunline armies that can't thin the advance, because the teleport-repositioning of Terminators and Mutilators constantly resets threat vectors and overloads static defensive positioning. It cracks open against elite alpha-strike lists that can delete key Terminator bricks before they engage, since losing the anchor units collapses both the scoring engine and the Dark Pact synergy simultaneously.
729: Built around waves of Cultist Mobs, Traitor Guardsmen, Accursed Cultists, and Dark Commune flooding objectives, backed by Chaos Bikers, Defilers, and Chaos Predator Destructors, all operating under Pactbound Zealots — where every melee model scores a Critical Hit on an unmodified 5+, dramatically increasing lethal hit frequency across the entire horde. This build punishes low-model-count armies that cannot clear objectives fast enough, as the sheer volume of lethal-hit-enabled attacks makes even cheap units disproportionately deadly in melee. It cracks under concentrated anti-horde firepower that clears screens before they can contest, exposing the relatively fragile heavy support elements to focus fire.
725: Built around Ravenwing Command Squads, Black Knights, Outrider Squads, Land Speeder Vengeances, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, and Land Speeders — the entire army is fast-moving ADEPTUS ASTARTES, all granted [ASSAULT] on ranged weapons by Company of Hunters, meaning nothing in this list stops shooting after advancing or falling back. It punishes slow, static gunlines that expect mobile armies to trade shooting for movement, since Company of Hunters eliminates that trade entirely. It cracks open against armies that can screen mid-board effectively and deny advance lanes, forcing the bikes into congested kill zones where their mobility advantage collapses.
637: Built around Land Speeder Vengeances, Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, and Azrael supported by Lion El'Jonson and a Lieutenant with combi-weapon, this is a mobile anti-armour gunline that floods the board with skimmer firepower from turn one. 642: Built around Deathwing Knights, Chaplains in Terminator Armour, Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, and Inner Circle Companions, this is a dense elite melee hammer that floods the board with high-durability Terminator-armoured bodies supported by Dark Angels' most powerful characters. 726: Built around Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and a fast Ravenwing cavalry screen of Command Squad, Sammael, Black Knights, and Outriders, all operating under Wrath of the Rock's detachment rule that subtracts 1 from wound rolls whenever an attacker's Strength exceeds the target's Toughness. It punishes armies that rely on mid-Strength shooting to crack Marine-tier Toughness, since that wound subtraction turns volume fire inefficient and forces opponents into overkill profiles. It cracks open against true anti-tank overload — high-AP, multi-damage weapons that are already wounding on 2s ignore the detachment's protection entirely, leaving the elite units exposed.
636: Built around Land Speeders, Land Speeder Vengances, Storm Speeders, Inner Circle Companions, and Librarians operating under the Librarius Conclave detachment, this is a fast, skimmer-heavy force that floods the board with mobile firepower backed by elite infantry. Armies that can screen out the skimmer access lanes or alpha-strike the fragile speeder chassis before the Disciplines activate will crack the list open, since losing even two or three speeders early collapses both the damage output and the board presence.
629: Built around Deathshroud Terminators, Lords of Contagion, Blightlord Terminators, Typhus, and bloated Poxwalker screens, this list weaponizes the Death Lord's Chosen detachment to steadily bleed opponents through mandatory end-of-phase mortal wound rolls against every Afflicted enemy unit — layering passive attrition on top of elite melee pressure. It punishes horde armies and low-save elite infantry brutally, since more Afflicted units means more dice rolling, and multiple small wounds overwhelm Feel No Pain stacking fast. Highly mobile or alpha-strike lists that can delete key Characters before Contagion establishes critical mass will crack it open, since the mortal wound engine collapses without the Afflicted tag applied at scale.
628: Built around Deathshroud Terminators, Lord of Contagion, Malignant Plaguecasters, Typhus, and bodies in Poxwalkers, Plague Marines, and Chaos Spawn, this list runs the Paragons of Putrescence detachment to push Contagion Range out to 12" on every Death Guard Character, blanketing the midfield in Contagion auras from turn one. The win condition is layered attrition: stack Contagion across multiple units simultaneously, grind opponents down through accumulated lethality while Myphitic Blight-Haulers provide mobile anti-armour pressure and screening chaff holds objectives long enough for the disease engine to pay out. It punishes slow, durable armies that want to trade in the midfield, because those opponents have to sit inside the Contagion bubble long enough to rot. Highly mobile or elite deep-strike lists crack it open by bypassing the aura envelope entirely, killing Characters before the Contagion web is established.
701: Built around Deathwatch Veterans, Deathwatch Terminators, Intercessors, and dual Librarians, this list leans heavily on elite infantry with psychic support across a fragmented detachment spread — most commonly the Firestorm Assault Force, which grants all Adeptus Astartes ranged weapons Assault and +1 Strength within 12", rewarding aggressive short-range positioning. The plan is to push elite kill-units into mid-table, exploit the Strength bonus to punch through tough targets, and use Librarians to toggle psychic disciplines — Divination for consistency, Biomancy for mobility — depending on matchup needs. It punishes horde and gunline armies by stacking high-volume, Assault-buffed fire from Veterans and Terminators at close range where the Strength bonus fully activates. It cracks open against alpha-strike and fast melee threats that strip the Veterans before they close, as the list's scoring engine depends on elite infantry surviving long enough to reach optimal range.
744: Built around Defilers, Maulerfiends, Lords Exultant, Infractors, Tormentors, Daemon Princes with Wings, Noise Marines, Flawless Blades, and Rhino-transported infantry, Coterie of the Conceited is a high-pressure mid-board brawler that floods every lane with threats simultaneously. The engine runs on the detachment's pledge mechanic — accurately predicting kills each round converts aggression directly into Pact points, rewarding lists that can guarantee destruction on demand rather than just threatening it. This build punishes slower, tankier armies through mobile anti-armour overload, with Maulerfiends and Defilers cracking heavy targets while infantry waves mop up, making efficient kill-counting trivially achievable. Spread-thin or horde-suppression builds that can't answer multiple large chassis in the same turn will find the pledge engine self-sustaining, but anything that alpha-strikes the Lords Exultant or denies early kills disrupts the Pact economy before it stabilises.
746: Built around Lords Exultant buffing waves of Infractors and Tormentors delivered by Chaos Rhinos, backed by Maulerfiends, Defilers, Flawless Blades, Daemon Princes, and Chaos Spawn, this list runs Peerless Bladesmen with Spectacle of Slaughter to chain Fights First and post-charge Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1 across every combat phase. The plan is to crash transports into mid-table, disgorge infantry into charges, and let the Lethal Hits/Sustained Hits selection delete priority targets before the opponent can respond, while Maulerfiends threaten armour on independent vectors. It punishes mid-range brawler lists that want to trade efficiently in melee, because Fights First on Flawless Blades and the charge-trigger buffs flip the combat math brutally against anything expecting a fair fight. It cracks when an opponent screens deep to deny charges, stranding expensive infantry in Rhinos while shooting them off the board before the melee engine can ignite.
743: Built around Noise Marines and Flawless Blades infantry ferried forward in Chaos Rhinos, supported by Lord Kakophonists, Tormentors, a winged Daemon Prince, and Lucius the Eternal, this list runs Spectacle of Slaughter to give Flawless Blades a Fights First guarantee, with Peerless Bladesmen layering Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1 onto charging units in over half of lists. The plan is to deliver multiple infantry bricks into the mid-table simultaneously, using Rhino transports to protect and accelerate the charge, then leverage Fights First and charge bonuses to trade up in melee while Noise Marines provide ranged pressure from behind. It punishes slow, elite armies that cannot avoid combat, where Fights First and stacking charge abilities systematically dismantle expensive units before they can swing. It struggles against fast shooting lists that strip the Rhinos early and strand the infantry in the open, neutering the charge engine before it ever engages.
572: Built around Purestrain Genestealers, Aberrants led by Abominants, and a Patriarch, running Biosanctic Broodsurge to stack charge bonuses and extra attacks on anything that makes contact. The plan is to deliver multiple elite melee threats simultaneously — Purestrains and Aberrant blobs charging in with boosted Attacks on the same turn while Neophyte Hybrids and Achilles Ridgerunners hold and contest objectives behind them. It punishes gunlines and low-model-count armies that can't screen every approach, because the sheer volume of charging bodies across multiple threat vectors overwhelms targeted removal. It cracks open against alpha-strike lists or anything with strong fight-last or pile-in denial, since the entire engine depends on actually completing the charge and the Biosanctic bonus only fires after the charge move lands.
754: Built around Nemesis Dreadknights, a Grand Master in Nemesis Dreadknight, Paladin Squads, and mobile infantry screens of Strike, Interceptor, Brotherhood Terminators, and Purifiers, running Argent Assault as its defining detachment with Banishers available as a secondary layer in most lists. The engine is a layered melee kill chain: Argent Assault's wound bonus activates when Paladins swing into high-Toughness targets where their Strength falls short, while Banishers' Leadership-test fight buffs — Sustained Hits on Psychic melee weapons — stack additional damage onto Dreadknight charges, scoring through raw combat attrition rather than cagey objective plays. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't sustain anti-tank overload against multiple Dreadknight threats simultaneously while mobile infantry repositions for secondaries. Boards with aggressive ranged chip damage that degrades Paladins before they close, or anything that floods the midfield to deny Interceptor teleport angles, can crack this open by starving the melee engine of clean targets.
753: Built around Castellan Crowe, multiple Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Purifier Squads, Strike Squads, and Brotherhood Terminators, this list runs Warpbane Task Force to turn Purifier positioning into a mobile Hallowed Ground engine that follows the army across the table. The win condition is zone control through objective saturation — Purifiers project Hallowed Ground out of your deployment zone and into No Man's Land, unlocking further benefits once you hold at least half those mid-table markers, so the list scores by physically dominating the centre with durable, layered infantry backed by Dreadknight muscle. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear waves of Grey Knight bodies contesting every angle simultaneously. It cracks when fast, high-volume anti-infantry shooting or blast weapons delete Purifier units before they can establish mid-board presence, collapsing the Hallowed Ground footprint the entire scoring engine depends on.
740: Built around Deathwatch Kill Teams, Imperial Navy Breachers, Subductor Squads, Sanctifiers, Aquila Kill Teams, and a constellation of Inquisitors (Kroyle and Draxus) supported by Watch Masters, Navigators, and Rogue Trader Entourages, this is a dense, multi-layered infantry swarm running Imperialis Fleet with Clandestine Operation to maximize command flexibility. The plan is to flood the board with cheap, resilient bodies across transports and on foot, using Imperialis Fleet's Eliminate At All Costs to focus the entire army's firepower onto a single priority target each turn while holding objectives through sheer unit volume. It punishes lists that rely on killing a small number of key pieces, because there are simply too many independent units to efficiently trade into, and layered screening makes alpha-strike deep strike threats work hard for every kill. However, the lack of concentrated elite hitting power means durable, high-toughness deathball lists can weather the focused fire and grind the swarm down on attrition.
756: Built around Purgation Squads, Purifier Squads, Strike Squads, Castellan Crowe, and multiple Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, this list splits evenly between Fires of Purgation and Warpbane Task Force detachments — one leaning on Righteous Persecution to pin and battle-shock enemy units, the other using Purifier positioning to extend Hallowed Ground across the board. The win condition is sustained ranged suppression: Purgation Squads lock down key threats through pinning while Dreadknights provide mobile firepower and melee reach to punish anything that survives the shooting phase. It excels against horde armies and infantry-dense lists, where layered shooting combined with battle-shock cascades degrades opponent efficiency before they can contest objectives meaningfully. It struggles against elite low-model-count forces that shrug off battle-shock, or aggressive alpha-strike builds that can close the distance and overwhelm the gunline before it establishes board control.
761: Built around Armiger Helverins, Armiger Warglaives, and a Knight Crusader, this list pairs a swarm of fast, expendable Armigers with a heavy-hitting centerpiece Walker, almost always running Valourstrike Lance alongside the core detachment. The engine is the Bondsman loop: when Armigers are buffed by a Bondsman ability, their ranged attacks gain Ignores Cover, letting the Helverins' autocannon volleys and the Crusader's mixed battery punish targets that would otherwise hide behind terrain, while the Advance-and-fire synergy from Valourstrike Lance keeps the whole force mobile without sacrificing shooting output. This combination punishes dug-in elite infantry and multi-wound vehicle lists that rely on cover saves to survive, stripping their protection before delivering layered anti-armour damage across multiple activations. It cracks open against high-volume mortal wound output or armies that can stack dedicated anti-tank fast enough to pick apart the Armigers before the Bondsman buffs come online.
522:
Built around Cthonian Beserks, Berehk Stornbröw, Ûthar the Destined, and Einhyr Hearthguard, this list uses the Dêlve Assault Shift to give Beserks Deep Strike, flooding mid-board and close quarters with hard-hitting melee infantry backed by a durable gunline of Hekaton Land Fortresses and Hearthkyn Warriors.

The plan is to drop Beserks directly onto contested objectives while the gunline holds flanks, using Ûthar and Hearthguard's re-roll wounds within 9" to punish anything that survives the initial charge and grind out scoring through sustained close-range pressure.

It punishes slower, less mobile elite armies that can't prevent the multi-angle Beserk drops from controlling the mid-table at once.

Swarm lists and anything with strong overwatch or pre-game screening can collapse the Deep Strike timing, and without a reliable counter to board-wide denial the list struggles to manufacture clean landing zones against disciplined opponents.
579: Built around Doomsday Arks, Canoptek Wraiths, Skorpekh Lords leading Skorpekh Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Flayed Ones, and Hexmark Destroyers under Awakened Dynasty — where Characters leading units add 1 to every Hit roll — this list plays like a multi-headed hammer that arrives from multiple vectors simultaneously. It wins by flooding the mid-board with durable, hitting-harder melee threats while Doomsday Arks punish anything stationary or lightly screened at range, forcing opponents into lose-lose positioning choices. Enaegic Dermal Bond on a key character, Technomancer support, and Canoptek Reanimators create a resilience layer that punishes attrition-focused lists unable to delete targets cleanly in one activation. It struggles against alpha-strike armies and high-volume mortal wound output that bypass its reanimation engines before the mobile threats can reach their intended targets.
739: Built around Lokhust Lords leading Lokhust Destroyers and Ophydian Destroyers under Awakened Dynasty, with Nekrosor Ammentar, Canoptek Wraiths, Skorpekh Lord, and the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon filling out a deep roster of mobile threats. The Awakened Dynasty's +1 to Hit on CHARACTER-led units means every Destroyer squad is swinging at full efficiency, while Veil of Darkness repositions key units to delete priority targets or contest objectives in unexpected angles. This build punishes static gunlines and elite low-model-count armies by flooding them with multiple high-accuracy kill vectors they cannot all answer in one turn. It struggles against heavy board-wide screening and alpha-strike pressure that can strip Characters before Canoptek Reanimators cycle wounds back, collapsing the hit-bonus engine mid-game.
767: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, massed Boyz squads, Painboyz, Gretchin screens, Kommandos, Wazdakka Gutsmek, Warboss characters, and Zodgrod Wortsnagga, this list runs both Equatorial Hordes and Freebooter Krew to push an overwhelming green tide forward with early Scouts 6" repositioning on key units. The win condition is seizing and locking the Freebooter Krew loot objective each Command phase while flooding the midboard with Sustained Hits 1 attacks across every Orks Infantry, Mounted, and Walker model, generating a volume of hits that bleeds opponents dry. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot match the sheer attrition of wave after wave of Sustained Hits infantry backed by Painboy healing. It cracks open against armies with reliable mass board control or high-AP shooting that can strip Boyz blobs before they reach melee range.
557: Built around Beast Snagga Boyz, Squighog Boyz, Beastboss, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Mozrog Skragbad, Kill Rig, and Ghazghkull Thraka, with Gretchin and Boyz providing layered screening mass, this is a wall-to-wall melee horde running Equatorial Hordes and Freebooter Krew detachments. The plan is to Scouts 6" selected MOB units into early threat range, flood the midboard, then weaponize Freebooter Krew's loot objective mechanic to force opponents off key markers while Beast Snagga units and mounted hammers grind through anything that contests. It punishes elite low-model armies that can't match the sheer volume of bodies and attacks, especially when Sustained Hits 1 fires across Infantry, Mounted, and Walker units simultaneously to overwhelm efficient defensive lines. Armies that alpha-strike the mounted hammers before the Scouts move resolves, or that screen the midboard tightly enough to deny the Beast Snagga charge lanes, can crack the engine before it gets rolling.
683: Built around waves of Intercessors, Heavy Intercessors, and Librarians, this Bastion Task Force list leans into the detachment's core rule: Adeptus Astartes Battleline units can shoot, charge, and perform Actions after Advancing or Falling Back, turning every infantry squad into a flexible scoring and fighting piece simultaneously. Librarians cycle through Psychic Disciplines each battle round — typically Divination for re-rolls or Biomancy for extra movement — to amplify whichever battleline unit needs the boost most. The build punishes static gunlines and horde armies by flooding the board with durable, action-completing infantry that never sacrifice mobility for output, making it nearly impossible to deny scoring through zone pressure alone. It struggles against elite alpha-strike lists or heavy anti-infantry volume that can delete squads before they act, since the power of the detachment relies on units surviving long enough to benefit from their post-move flexibility.
554: Built around Kayvaan Shrike, Aethon Shaan, assault intercessors and vanguard veterans with jump packs, inceptors, centurion devastators, and a dense screen of scouts, incursors, and intercessors, all operating under Shadowmark Talon's blanket cover-at-range protection. The plan is to deny enemy shooting with that passive cover save while the jump pack elements ingress and pressure objectives mid-board, backed by centurion devastators hammering armour and Shaan's free Into Darkness triggering key repositions at zero CP cost. It punishes gunline-heavy lists that rely on volume ranged fire at range, since nearly every unit gets cover unless enemies close within 12"—forcing opponents into unfavorable positioning. It struggles against lists that can reliably close that 12" gap or alpha-strike through melee, since the passive durability evaporates in close range and the jump pack threat pieces are fragile if caught before they engage.
760: Built around Logan Grimnar, Arjac Rockfist, multiple squads of Wolf Guard Terminators, Terminator Assault squads, and Bjorn the Fell-Handed, with Intercessors providing midfield bodies, this is a transport-heavy terminator hammer running primarily the Saga of the Great Wolf detachment. The plan is to deliver multiple elite terminator payloads into mid-table brawls simultaneously, using Logan's leadership to amplify the Hunting Pack rotations — cycling Encircling Jaws for threat extension via re-rolled charges and advances to ensure the kill trains land on target every turn. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot absorb repeated heavy-armour engagements, particularly those relying on single hard targets that both Bjorn and stacked terminator weight can overload in one activation. Boards with robust screening infrastructure and long-range anti-tank volume that can strip the transport layer before deployment completes will crack this list open before the brawl engine engages.
759: Built around Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, multiple squads of Wolf Guard Terminators, and Arjac Rockfist, this list runs Saga of the Great Wolf to deliver a fist-heavy terminator hammer into the opponent's face, often delivered via Land Raider Redeemer with a Captain and Lieutenant stacked inside for reroll support. The win condition is straightforward violence: activate the right Hunting Pack to surge terminators up the board, crash them into the opponent's scoring units, and physically remove threats before they can score. It punishes horde and mid-table brawler lists badly, using massed elite melee to simply delete whatever holds the center. The weakness is anything that can strip the Redeemer before it delivers its cargo or kite the terminators with fast, durable objective holders that force them to overextend.
773: Built around Tzaangor Enlightened, Sekhetar Robots, Scarab Occult Terminators, Rubric Marines, Sorcerers, Daemon Princes with wings, and Defilers, this list floods the board with layered bodies across multiple threat categories simultaneously. The win condition is attrition through volume — Enlightened and Robots contest and trade efficiently while Terminators and Daemon Princes punch through elite targets, leaving opponents unable to address every threat before primary points bleed away. It punishes gunlines and low-model-count armies that cannot generate enough high-damage attacks to clear the mass of bodies quickly, particularly struggling against the Rubricae's resilience to Damage 1 weapons under the Rubricae Phalanx detachment. Armies that can deliver concentrated high-Damage output or flood the midboard with equally numerous screens will crack it open by denying the trade efficiency the list depends on.
771: Built around Sorcerers in Terminator Armour buffing Scarab Occult Terminators, Sekhetar Robots, Rubric Marines, and Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, with Magnus anchoring roughly half of all lists as a centrepiece beatstick, this is a mass-model psychic gunline that floods the table with durable bodies across every threat range. The win condition is layered psychic firepower — Fatecaster Greatbows carpeting mid-field while Scarab Occult and Robots punish anyone who advances into range — backed by relentless objective presence from near-unkillable Rubric screens. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot trade efficiently into multiple durable, redundant units simultaneously. It struggles against aggressive alpha-strike lists that can isolate and delete key Terminator blobs before Sorcerer buffs come online.
772: Built around Magnus the Red, a winged Daemon Prince, Scarab Occult Terminators, and a deep bench of Rubric Marines, Tzaangor Enlightened, Tzaangors, Chaos Spawn, Sekhetar Robots, and Sorcerers operating inside Grand Coven, this is a mass-horde psychic army with genuine elite punch. The plan is to flood the board with bodies — screens of Tzaangors and Chaos Spawn protecting scoring infantry — while Magnus and the Daemon Prince delete priority targets with boosted psychic firepower, with Grand Coven's Imbued Manifestation extending psychic range to reach across the board before opponents can close. It punishes slow gunlines and low-model-count elite lists that can't clear the sheer volume of cheap bodies fast enough to contest objectives. It cracks open against fast melee armies that can bypass the screens and reach the infantry blocks before the psychic engine can answer them turn one.
774: Built around Sekhetar Robots, Defilers, Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with Wings, Forgefiends, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, Tzaangors, Tzaangor Shaman, and Magnus the Red, running Hexwarp Thrallband and Sekhetar Cohort — a layered psychic construct army that floods the board with robots whose attacks gain the Psychic keyword and whose melee hits sharper while near friendly Psykers. The gameplan is to dominate No Man's Land objective control early, locking in the Hexwarp Thrallband's Flow of Magic across the midboard to amplify the robot swarms, while Defilers and Forgefiends hammer armour at range and the Daemon Prince applies surgical pressure. It brutally punishes elite low-model-count lists that can't match the volume of Psychic-tagged attacks landing across multiple activations and threat vectors simultaneously. It cracks open against armies that can deny midboard objective control early, collapsing the Flow of Magic uptime and stranding the robot blobs without their full Psyker-aura support.
780: Built around Magnus the Red, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Chaos Spawn screens, and a supporting cast of Sorcerers and a Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with Wings, this Grand Coven list plays a layered psychic gunline that floods the board with bodies. The engine is the Grand Coven's rotating Command phase abilities — Imbued Manifestation extends psychic weapon ranges to punish enemies who think they're safe at mid-board, while the threat of Psychic Maelstrom forces opponents to respect the entire firing line, letting Magnus and the Terminators delete priority targets while Rubric Marines and Spawn hold ground. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't contest multiple objectives simultaneously against a horde that also carries genuine long-range psychic firepower. Armies that can close fast and get into melee before the Coven abilities cycle — or that outrange the extended psychic profiles entirely — can strip the gunline before it fully activates.
764: Built around Norn Assimilators, Norn Emissaries, Maleceptors, Psychophages, Biovores, Neurotyrant, Swarmlord, and Neurolictors, this list uses the Talons of the Norn Queen detachment to unlock Protean Purpose on its Norn units while Crusher Stampede rewards damaged Monsters with bonus hit and wound rolls, turning attrition into offensive output. The win condition is layered ranged pressure from Biovores and Maleceptors softening targets while Norn Assimilators and Psychophages close into mid-board, threatening objectives and forcing unfavorable trades at every range band. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't contest multiple threat vectors simultaneously, as the sheer volume of durable Monsters overwhelms focused anti-tank overload strategies. Massed mortal-wound output or high-volume shooting that strips Monsters below Starting Strength before Crusher Stampede triggers cracks it open, and fast alpha-strike armies that seize mid-board before the gunline stabilizes cause serious problems.
597: Built around Norn Emissaries, Norn Assimilators, Neurotyrants, Maleceptors, Zoanthropes, Neurolictor screens, and Biovore artillery, this is a Synaptic Nexus list that weaponizes the Talons of the Norn Queen's Protean Purpose ability to reshape its Norn monsters into whatever tool the game state demands. The plan is to keep key threats inside Synapse Range to cycle Synaptic Imperatives each round, using the Norn units' adaptive profiles to crack armor, grind midboard brawls, or punish overextension while Biovores chip screens from safety. It punishes lists that rely on a single defensive posture — static gunlines or castle deployments — because the Protean Purpose flexibility means no single counter-tech reliably neuters the whole army. The weakness is consistency: at roughly half win rate, lists that flood the board with durable bodies or generate pressure faster than the Synapse engine can adapt will expose how tempo-dependent the cycling mechanic truly is.
765: Built around Trygons (often upgraded to Trygon Primes via Enhancement), Raveners, Hyperadapted Raveners, The Red Terror, Neurotyrant, Zoanthropes, Maleceptors, Biovores, Tyrannofexes, The Swarmlord, Neurolictor, and Hormagaunts operating under the Subterranean Assault detachment, which grants Trygons and Mawlocs the Burrower keyword and lets up to two Trygons take Enhancements and the Warlord slot. The plan is to combine deep-striking Burrower threats with a synapse-heavy psychic/gunline backfield, using Trygons and Raveners to crack open mid-board positions while Biovores and Tyrannofexes grind from range and Hormagaunts screen objectives. It punishes castle-heavy or low-mobility lists that can't respond to simultaneous threats from underground and the front line, forcing priority overload across multiple vectors. It struggles against elite, mobile armies that can screen deep strike zones effectively, neutralize the Trygon delivery system before it hits, and simply outgun the relatively average-efficiency shooting at range.
763: Built around Lictors, Trygons, Hormagaunts, Neurotyrant, Zoanthropes, Biovores, the Swarmlord, and a deep supporting cast of Maleceptors, Haruspex, and Hyperadapted Raveners under Subterranean Assault, which grants Trygons the Burrower keyword and lets up to two be designated as Characters capable of taking Enhancements — most lists run a Trygon Prime as Warlord. The plan is to flood every midboard angle simultaneously: Lictors and Neurolictor infiltrate forward to deny space and enable subsequent arrivals, while Burrower Trygons and Raveners erupt from underground to overwhelm priority targets and contest objectives before the opponent can consolidate. It punishes slow, static gunlines that cannot reposition quickly enough to handle threats arriving from multiple vectors at once. Armies that can screen underground deployment zones, apply early attrition to the infiltrating vanguard, or out-trade the individually fragile assault units in the midgame crack this list open before its tempo snowballs.
762: Built around paired Broodlords leading double squads of Genestealers, supported by Tyrannofexes and Norn Emissaries for fire support, with Swarmlord, Neurotyrant, Maleceptor, Lictors, and Hormagaunts rounding out a deep, flexible roster across Invasion Fleet. The plan is to flood multiple angles simultaneously — Lictors set up Genestealer charges from unexpected vectors while Biovores and Tyrannofexes punish anything that bunkers up, creating a kill-or-be-killed threat web that scores through board control and attrition. This list punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't absorb multi-directional pressure from hard-hitting melee hammers and layered ranged fire at once. It cracks open against aggressive alpha-strike lists that can delete the Genestealer units before they engage, stripping the close-combat engine before the threat web ever materializes.
611: Built around Khorne Berzerkers, Exalted Eightbound, Eightbound, Slaughterbound, and Jakhals screening for Khârn and Angron, all delivered through Chaos Rhinos and Chaos Spawn bubble-wrap, this is a wall-to-wall melee army running Berzerker Warband — every unit that charges gains +1 Attack and +2 Strength on all melee weapons, turning even mediocre swings into lethal contact. The plan is simple and violent: crash into midboard turn one, use Rhino-mounted Berzerkers and screening Jakhals to lock opponents off objectives while Exalted Eightbound and Angron delete anything that matters. It punishes slow, static armies with poor melee defence — any list that relies on holding ground with moderate-toughness units gets buried under charge-buffed volume that outweights nearly any conventional screen. It cracks against shooting-heavy armies that can strip the Rhinos early and force charges into prepared positions, denying the charge bonus when it matters most.
